title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Hanoi: Meet in the Middle
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra slice through Hanoi’s Hoàn Kiếm street graph by expanding shortest paths from both start and finish. The two search frontiers advance until they meet, often cutting exploration time dramatically.
ig_caption:
🗺️⚡ **Bidirectional Dijkstra** in Hanoi (Hoàn Kiếm)

Instead of running one long Dijkstra from the start, this visualization grows two priority-queue frontiers at the same time: one forward from the source and one backward from the destination. When the frontiers meet at a node (or edge), the algorithm stitches the partial shortest paths together to recover the optimal route. ✅

📌 **Deep graph-theory view (real street maps):**
Road networks form a weighted graph (nodes = intersections, edges = street segments with costs like distance/time). Bidirectional Dijkstra leverages the symmetry of shortest-path optimality by reducing the explored region in the graph—effectively searching from both ends and stopping early when the best-known connection is provably optimal.

🔥 Want to see the frontier waves collide? Tap to watch the “middle meeting” moment, then save this reel for later.

🚦 **Hanoi street routing with Bidirectional Dijkstra**
Graph search is all about finding the lowest-cost path across weighted edges—think intersections as nodes and road segments as connections. This video shows how Bidirectional Dijkstra improves efficiency by expanding from both the start and the goal simultaneously until the best path is determined.
